P1.evidence: Frame delivered as three parts, not four - 'dive into what your goal is, where you're currently at, see how we can fit in there, and if we can even fit in there' - no 'what's in the way' or 'what you need'. Agreement taken ('okay?' - 'Great, that sounds good'). Open question run verbatim: 'so take me through, like, how can we potentially help you?'. Application notes were referenced but only 40 minutes in ('I think I read something with a wedding. Is that correct?'), not read back at the open.

P2.evidence: Age/height/weight asked, though late and self-flagged: 'I actually completely forgot to go over that... what's your specific age, like height, and also weight'. Injuries probed properly (tendinitis, knee, hip). Diet interrogated in real detail including eating window. Work was never asked - the prospect volunteered 'I work outside of the home, so I'm moving every day'. Health conditions, sleep and daily energy were never asked at all; the prospect volunteered the sleep detail unprompted ('when I eat too late, I also don't sleep great').

P3.evidence: Strongest phase. Aesthetic goal driven to specifics ('getting those abs popping and getting your arms and chest a little bit bigger'), mobility and flexibility scaled 1-10. Deeper why surfaced cleanly: 'There's usually also a deeper why just personally to it?' produced the wedding and then the real answer, 'a kind of quiet confidence that comes from it'. Legacy reached via wedding and kids. 'Who else does that impact' was tacked onto a question rather than asked ('and probably, of course, also your wife') and never pursued with the fiancee - a costly omission given she became the blocker. Reflect-back was a factual recap rather than the 'this isn't really about X' reframe.

P4.evidence: Past attempts covered thoroughly: gym, at-home equipment, three years of self-coaching, and 'in those three years, do you feel like you've made a lot of progress for yourself?' - 'No, not a ton.' Root cause probed with 'So what stopped you from getting that so far, do you think?' and 'what do you feel like stopped you from reaching out to a coach before?'. Prospect named the gap himself as knowledge and expertise. The scripted 'the information isn't the problem' line was not run - reasonably, since here the information genuinely is the gap.

P5.evidence: Consequence question was asked but on a short horizon and had to be repeated because the prospect misheard: 'if it sort of keeps going, like it's been going for the last three years'. The willingness-to-settle move was asserted rather than asked - 'it doesn't sound like you're actually willing to settle for not finding that' - so the prospect never had to say it himself. No 'why not' follow-up and no line-in-the-sand. The rep then softened the whole frame: 'the reason I actually asked that question wasn't to put you in a position of not doing it'.

P6.evidence: Belief question run well before presenting: 'You have the knowledge and the expertise behind you, and someone in your corner is actually going to push you... do you think you actually follow through with that?' - 'Yes. Yeah, definitely.' The go-all-in isolation was run as a 1-10 scale AFTER the programme walkthrough rather than as a pre-presentation commitment check, and it surfaced price as the open item. The rep proceeded to price anyway rather than returning to Phase 5, which is exactly where the call then stalled.

P11.evidence: Close attempted and payment sought via a refundable holding deposit - 'we usually just put on a small [deposit]... If your wife's like, no, absolutely, we're not doing this, we would just put that back' - which the prospect declined. No payment collected, so onboarding, agreement signature and welcome-email steps could not be reached. The rep did secure and confirm a live calendar invite for the follow-up.

objection_plays.detail: Ran the softer half: confirmed she knew about the call, confirmed she was supportive, and asked what her reaction to 6k would be. Ran the fallback deposit move including the refund condition. Did NOT run the three moves that do the work - 'money aside, do you personally feel this CAN get you to your goal', 'is there any reason she would NOT want you stronger', and above all 'is this genuinely needing her input, or asking permission to bet on yourself / is that responsibility hers or yours'. He accepted the household spending rule at face value and converted the objection into a booked joint call instead.

'Sleep on it overnight in terms of cost' is a textbook think-it-over trigger. The rep isolated it to cost, which is a good first move, but then ran none of the play - no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you there', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'when do you make a different decision'. He pivoted straight to the spouse conversation and to scheduling.

Budget was named as the live blocker - 'in planning a wedding, we have a budget that we're working through' and 'before I spend 6k'. None of the open-wallet play ran: no finances-aside isolation, no should-I-versus-how reframe, no 'most clients pay upfront but for some we break it up', and no financial picture at all - no cash on hand, monthly surplus, cards or investments. A payment plan was never mentioned to a prospect whose only stated obstacle was a short-term wedding budget.

notes: Excellent discovery and root-cause work, weak back half. The single coachable moment: at the 1-10 check the prospect said nine with price as the only gap, and the rep went to price without returning to Phase 5 to harden the commitment. Then, with budget named explicitly, he never opened the wallet conversation or mentioned instalments - he defaulted to rescheduling. He also never asked about the fiancee anywhere in Phase 3, so when she surfaced as the decision-maker he had nothing built.
